text.p: The chairman of Israel's Aladdin Knowledge Systems Ltd said Thursday he was comfortable with an analyst's projection of $0.83 in earnings per share this year.

The executive, Yanki Margalit, also said he was comfortable with an EPS projection of $1.05 for 1998. Both forecasts were made by Josephtal Lyon and Ross analysts Robert Goldman and Abraham Finkelstein.
"I feel comfortable with these numbers. They make a lot of sense," he told Reuters at a conference on Israeli companies sponsored by Josephtal Lyon and Ross.
"If you only look at the first quarter (1997) results, I think (the 1997 figure) is pretty much in line and even over the expectation you see here."

The company, a developer of products that protect software against piracy, reported 1996 earnings per share of $0.69 without charges on operating income of $1.6 million. The EPS for the first quarter of 1997 were $0.22 on income of $2.2 million.
The company's major product lines are the HASP and Hardlock protection systems and Margalit said he expected to expand the company's so-called smart card segment starting this year.
The card is a plastic card carrying information on a computer chip that can be used for such things as identification and credit operations.
The segment was a "minor, even negligible," part of 1996's $29 million in revenues.
It should reach $1.5 million in sales this year "and next year will be an even more interesting year for us," he said.
